title: When the Clock Falls
premise: In a river town on the edge of an empire, Ulyana Okonkwo, apprentice to the late mapmaker Vasyl Okonkwo, is completing the atlas he died protecting when a sealed letter surfaces naming their family among conspirators the authorities are hunting. As informants circle and the workshop is marked for seizure, Ulyana must decide whether to burn the atlas or finish it, knowing each finished plate is both evidence of treason and proof that the erased places existed. With help from a disgraced archivist and the master's estranged daughter, they race to complete and smuggle the atlas out before the spring ice breaks, when the river will open the town to soldiers. The atlas escapes by water; the workshop burns; Ulyana survives, no longer invisible, carrying the memory—and the cost—of what was saved.
about_author: I. M. Nystrom is the pen name of a former cartographic archivist who spent a decade cataloguing maps confiscated from private collections. They write historical fiction about the people history forgets to name.

chapters.title: The Unfinished Coastline
chapters.summary: Ulyana's POV. Winter deepens over the mapmaker's workshop where Ulyana inks the final plates of Master Vasyl's atlas alone, keeping his death quiet to avoid seizure of his estate. The emotional beat is grief disguised as diligence—the comfort of routine, and the first crack in it when a coastline refuses to match any source.

chapters.title: A Letter Under the Floor
chapters.summary: Ulyana's POV. Repairing a warped floorboard, Ulyana finds a sealed letter in Vasyl's hand naming the Okonkwo family as keepers of 'the evidence' for a conspiracy of scholars and smugglers. Fear arrives like cold water: staying invisible was never an option. The beat is dread and reluctant inheritance.

chapters.title: The Man Who Counts Windows
chapters.summary: Ulyana's POV. A government surveyor begins measuring buildings along the river street, lingering at the workshop, asking questions about its former master. Ulyana lies badly, then learns from a neighbor that informants are paid per name. The beat is paranoia tightening like a vise.

chapters.title: What the Archivist Kept
chapters.summary: Danylo's POV. A disgraced imperial archivist, Danylo, arrives claiming Vasyl owed him the atlas—or at least a copy. He reveals the conspiracy was a network preserving records of villages the empire erased. Ulyana must choose between distrusting him and needing him. The beat is wary alliance.

chapters.title: The Daughter Who Left
chapters.summary: Kateryna's POV. Vasyl's estranged daughter returns for the funeral she missed, intending only to sell the property. Reading her father's letter, she recognizes his handwriting in the atlas margins and understands why he chose maps over family. The beat is resentment curdling into resolve.

chapters.title: Plates for the Fire
chapters.summary: Ulyana's POV. The surveyor returns with a seizure order pending; Kateryna urges burning the atlas, Danylo urges finishing it. Ulyana works through the night on the erased villages' plates, discovering Vasyl hid coordinates inside decorative borders. The beat is defiant purpose born of fear.

chapters.title: Ice Groaning on the River
chapters.summary: Danylo's POV. Danylo arranges passage with a smuggler who owes the conspiracy a debt, but the price is betrayal: he must hand over one name besides his own. He gives a false one, knowing it condemns an innocent stranger. The beat is guilt as the cost of survival made explicit.

chapters.title: The Night of Seals
chapters.summary: Kateryna's POV. Officials seal the workshop doors with wax and lead while the trio hides inside, finishing the last plate by candle stub. Kateryna signs her father's colophon in his stead. The beat is claustrophobic climax-building—work as resistance, breath held against authority.

chapters.title: Before the Ice Breaks
chapters.summary: Ulyana's POV. Climax. At dawn the trio slips the atlas into a smuggler's skiff through a gap in the ice as the surveyor discovers them. The workshop is set alight in the chaos—Kateryna's choice, not an accident. Ulyana watches the atlas vanish downstream as ash rises. The beat is sacrifice and release.

chapters.title: A Map Without Borders
chapters.summary: Ulyana's POV. Weeks later, word arrives that the atlas reached a printing house abroad; copies will circulate under no one's name. Ulyana, now teaching a new apprentice in another town, draws a coastline from memory and lets the student finish it. The beat is quiet resolution: memory survives by being handed on.
